clue.text: Mug and flag held by jockey

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: to jockey for position is to compete, to vie
to flag is to droop or tire

explanation.surface: A racing scene: a mug and a flag being carried by a jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' reads as a rider but is the verb meaning compete; 'mug' is slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is informal slang for a person's face, and a visage is a literary word for the face.

clue.text: French writer displaying anger after dance

blocks.note: the volta is a lively Renaissance dance
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A French author loses their temper after a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the anger piece behind the dance piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire, author of Candide, was an Enlightenment author from France, so he exemplifies the definition.

clue.text: Speak about very old area of France

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for speak goes round the other letters

blocks.note: to speak is to say
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone lectures on an ancient part of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoy is a historic Alpine region of south-eastern France, once a duchy, so an example of a French area.

clue.text: Monstrous sisters, thugs holding Greek up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the abbreviation runs backwards
holding means keeping inside, so the thugs surround the Greek piece

blocks.note: goons are hired thugs
GR is the abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: Monstrous women, like thugs, holding up a Greek man in a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' reads as robbing, but splits into a container signal and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Gorgons were three sisters, Medusa among them, with snakes for hair.

clue.text: Peering across lake to make out bird

indicators.note: a word placed across another spans it, so the lake abbreviation sits within

blocks.note: peering is looking hard, staring
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone squints across a lake trying to identify a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Protestant let off scout

indicators.note: off means gone bad or not right, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Protestant boy scout is let off a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout' suggests the youth movement, but it is the person who seeks out gifted performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout in sport or entertainment looks for promising recruits, which is exactly a talent spotter's job.

clue.text: Further publication concerning children

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
issue is a legal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A sequel book about children.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a new release of a book or record previously published, so a further publication.

clue.text: Propose appalling reduction

indicators.note: appalling means dreadful, so the letters are mangled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a drastic, terrible cut in spending.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce a bill or motion is to put it forward for consideration, so to propose it.

clue.text: Dark logo to be changed - gracious me!

indicators.note: being changed means being altered, so the four letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: the letters of logo, rearranged
my! is an exclamation of surprise like gracious me!

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed that a company's sombre logo is being redesigned.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy describes poorly lit, dim surroundings, a synonym of dark.

clue.text: Cathedral city's organ fund

blocks.note: the liver is a body organ
a pool is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: A cathedral city raising money for a new church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the cathedral's musical instrument, but it is the body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool, in north-west England, has two cathedrals, Anglican and Catholic, so it qualifies as a cathedral city.

clue.text: At first glance, where are the chronometer's hands?

blocks.note: first meaning: judging by appearances
second meaning, literally: a watch's hands sit on its dial

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic question: the hands of a chronometer are found on its face, taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means judging by appearances, while a clock's face is literally where the hands are.

clue.text: Opening number covered by funky trio

indicators.note: something funky is offbeat and jumbled, so the three letters are rearranged
something covered by another is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: the letters of trio, rearranged
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A funk trio plays a cover version as its opening number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening number' looks like a single phrase for the definition, but only 'Opening' defines; 'number' supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or piece, a shortened form of introduction.

clue.text: Emergency accommodation when the weather's bad could be no party

indicators.note: could be suggests one possible form the letters may take, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of no party, rearranged
bad weather means one is in a storm

explanation.surface: A makeshift shelter in foul weather is hardly a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like one cryptic definition, but 'no party' rearranges to the first two words and the weather phrase supplies the last three.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says any refuge will do in a crisis, so the phrase names makeshift shelter taken in an emergency.

clue.text: Retort made by dealer, ultimately, to one after Ecstasy

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of dealer is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of dealer
I is the Roman numeral one
post is Latin for after, as in postwar
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sharp reply from a drug dealer to a customer chasing ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick clever reply, a synonym of a retort; originally a fencing counter-thrust.

clue.text: Confine drug dealer, clerical worker

blocks.note: to pen is to shut in
a pusher is a seller of illegal drugs

explanation.surface: Instructions to lock up a drug dealer, issued by an office worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pusher is a disparaging term for someone doing routine office paperwork.

clue.text: Increase pace in the saddle

blocks.note: a pace is a single step
a rider who is up is mounted, in the saddle

explanation.surface: A rider urges the horse faster once mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increase pace' reads as a single instruction; 'pace' actually belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up output or effort is to raise it, an idiomatic phrasal verb for increasing.

clue.text: Like a minister, playwright on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio, words are heard rather than read, so the name is taken by sound

blocks.note: J. B. Priestley wrote An Inspector Calls and was a famous radio broadcaster

explanation.surface: A clergyman-like dramatist being interviewed on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Priestley himself was well known for his wartime radio talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestly means characteristic of a priest, and a minister is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: In game, cracked riddle

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the six letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: During a game, someone has solved the riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' suits the riddle as solved, but it signals breaking the letters up.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzling mystery or puzzle, a close synonym of riddle.

clue.text: Found out from good editor about film director

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the editor pieces wrap around the director

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
ED is the abbreviation for editor
David Lean directed Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Gossip learnt from a kindly editor about a film director.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather information bit by bit, so gleaned means found out.

clue.text: Last longer than others where French water treated

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so the letters are worked into another order

blocks.note: ou is French for where
the letters of water, rearranged

explanation.surface: French tap water is treated, so it keeps longer than other supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to remain in use longer than it, i.e. to outlast it.

clue.text: Happens to drink after performance

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the drink piece is placed behind the performance piece

blocks.note: a turn is a short stage act
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: A performer heads for a drink after the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the drink piece behind the performance piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns up arises or occurs unexpectedly, an idiomatic sense of happening.

clue.text: Incendiary liquid mate used in Vietnam

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so the friend sits within the war abbreviation

blocks.note: 'Nam is American slang for Vietnam
a mate is a friend, a pal

explanation.surface: A grim reminder of the burning jelly dropped during the Vietnam War.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied petrol used in firebombs, an inflammable substance.

clue.text: Where bandits are likely to take your money?

definitions.text: Where bandits are likely to take your money?

blocks.clueFragment: Where bandits are likely to take your money
blocks.note: surface reading: a place haunted by robbers
setter's reading: one-armed bandits, the slot machines found in seaside gaming halls

explanation.surface: A warning about a lawless spot where robbers relieve travellers of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a fruit machine, and those are what fill a seaside gaming hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Such venues house coin-operated gambling machines that swallow visitors' money, so the 'bandits' are machines.

clue.text: Sense of anxiety in Penang state

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Unease felt in the Malaysian state of Penang.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is deep dread or apprehension, a German loanword for a feeling of unease.

clue.text: Article absorbing female drained of colour

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the article swallows the female pronoun

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece so gripping a woman went pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey and pale like ash, describing a face that has lost its colour.

clue.text: Vision of gift horse put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters are thrown into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sees a gift horse turned out to pasture, recalling the proverb about not looking it in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision here means foresight in planning: the ability to anticipate what will happen.

clue.text: Novelist from Maine, close to bachelor girl

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
the last letter of bachelor
Edith is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A writer from Maine lives near a single man's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith was a Victorian English novelist and poet, author of The Egoist.
explanation.definitionFit: George Meredith wrote novels such as The Egoist, so he is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a course beginning in York

indicators.note: a beginning is the start, so just the opening letter of the city is used

blocks.note: taken as written
a path is a course or route
the first letter of York

explanation.surface: A bored student shrugs off a course starting up in York.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, a state of not caring, which is the same as lacking interest.
